quest.title: Chronic Illness
quest.description: Yesterday did not quite end so well, so you and Paimon decide to go check on Collei.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x22775, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two. I was just about to go look for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Tighnari, what're you doing here? Where's Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I came to check on Collei's condition. To put it simply, she's not well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean she's sick? How could she be... Oh, wait a minute, could it be because of what Paimon did yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No, no need to worry. Something as small as you could never harm her. This sickness is something that Collei has been dealing with for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei has been more excited than usual since you two arrived — a little too much so, to be honest. She hasn't remembered to take care of herself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: *sigh* I suppose it's understandable, though. She hasn't been around anyone she considered a friend for some time now. It must have been refreshing for her to have you two here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Tighnari, what's really wrong with Collei...?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ahem, let's take this conversation elsewhere. Collei just fell asleep after taking her medicine. She needs some peace and quiet.

talks.objective: Follow Tighnari to discuss the details elsewhere

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, let's continue our conversation here, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: To be honest, I hadn't realized you're that Honorary Knight from Mondstadt until Collei told me just now. I've also heard all about your deeds in Liyue and Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So just to clarify, what I'm about to tell you about Collei is not because of who you are or your past feats. Instead, I am going to tell you because...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, because Collei asked me to.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And honestly speaking, I was against Collei revealing her past to you.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But, she insisted, saying you two treated her with sincerity and as a friend. So now she wishes to reciprocate the gesture.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Tighnari, what exactly is wrong with Collei? You said this is something she's been dealing with for some time. Just how serious is it?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Right, ever since she was a child, she's been afflicted with a disease called Eleazar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eleazar?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, it's a disease unique to the lands of Sumeru. It is characterized by dark and hardened scales that form on the body.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: At first, the afflicted may only feel mild numbness on affected areas of the skin. However, as the disease progresses, one may begin feeling fatigued and even experience peripheral paresthesia.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: In its final stages, the disease strips a person of the ability to control their own body, and they effectively become completely immobile.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds terrifying!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They'll lose all control over their body!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hold on! So when Collei seemed to be acting a little clumsy earlier, it was because...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Correct. That would be the effects of Eleazar, which is precisely why I do not want her carrying or holding anything, lest she ends up hurting herself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So is there any cure for Eleazar?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: With appropriate treatment, the disease can be effectively controlled before it progresses to a more serious stage. However, there is, unfortunately, still no true cure for Eleazar.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, Collei's mother still hoped that there was something out there. She handed Collei over to an organization known as the Fatui after one of their members lied and said they had a cure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? The Fatui!?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, it appears you already are familiar with them. That'll save me some explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, the person who eventually rescued Collei and brought her to me for care said that she had been given to a Harbinger known as "The Doctor."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I have no idea how this "Doctor" managed to do it, but her case of Eleazar was completely stable for all the years that Collei was with them.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: However, Collei's days with the Fatui were anything but pleasant.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei is a resilient individual and always tries to appear cheerful, but her experience with the Fatui has left deep scars. Even now, she can still feel deathly afraid of someone touching her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Paimon had no idea Collei's been through so much suffering...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, Paimon, Collei wanted me to tell you that she's sorry for scaring you yesterday. She also wanted both of you to know that she's sorry for hiding her illness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She doesn't need to apologize. None of this is her fault at all!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well said. I hope you'll get a chance to tell her that in person the next time you see her.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei once thought that it would be impossible for her to have any real friendships... I trust that you two will never let my trainee experience such emotional pain again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Tighnari! We'll take good care of her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's Collei's condition now?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, it's not too serious at this point. She over-exerted herself the last couple of days, which is what led to her break down this time. As long as she has taken her medicine and gets plenty of rest, she should get better.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Though, I must admit that Collei's condition was much more stable when she first arrived here in Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: She was interested in the work of the Forest Rangers the moment she saw us. I could see that she was serious about learning, so I felt compelled to ask her to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Her stamina has gotten much worse recently. Though a moderate amount of physical exercise is always necessary, I'm afraid the long-distance patrols are a little too much for her now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, now that I've told you about Collei's past, I think I'll head into the rainforest to find some ingredients needed for her medicine. I'll see you two later.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, can we come along?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We'd like to do something to help Collei, too!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, but I must warn you two, the rainforest is a dangerous place, especially for someone who's still recovering, like the Traveler. You must follow closely and listen to every instruction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problemo!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's go then. We'll be looking for a plant known as the Nilotpala Lotus. It's often used to help those afflicted with Eleazar recover their energy.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: There should be Nilotpala Lotuses growing somewhere in this area. Let's split up and begin searching.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If you could manage to gather four of them, that would be sufficient.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We'll rendezvous here once you've gathered the needed amount.

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: Tighnari, thank goodness we found you here. We were just about to head back and find you at Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Nasrin
dialogues.text: We just discovered a Withering Zone.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Withering is back!? But the patrol route you were on should have been already cleared just a week ago. It reappeared so quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Can you tell me the exact location?

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: It's up ahead, deep in the river valley. It's appeared in a spot that blocks nearly the entire narrow part of the valley area, so we decided to come find you as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And the radius of the contamination?

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: Sorry, I couldn't get a clear enough view to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Nasrin
dialogues.text: No one in our patrol team had a Vision, and it appeared to still be spreading, so we didn't risk getting any closer.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Okay, I understand. You made the right decision. I'll go deal with it right away. In the meantime, please guide {M#these two}{F#these two} back to Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Tighnari! Why don't you let us help you?

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: You two have only just arrived in Sumeru. You're still unfamiliar with many things in these lands.

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: There's a unique type of anomaly that occurs in the Sumeru rainforest. It's called "The Withering."

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: The affected areas not only cause nearby vegetation to wither, but it's also lethal to wildlife and even people. If you don't carry a Vision, then you should think twice before approaching such places.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, Amir is absolutely right. I wasn't kidding when I said the rainforest is a dangerous place.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As Amir said, only someone with a Vision — that is, the power to manipulate elements — will be able to resist The Withering's corrosive effects for a time.

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: That's right. If any of the Forest Rangers without a Vision come across a Withering Zone, we first make a record of the location and then have a ranger with the proper abilities deal with it, like Tighnari here.

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: Only someone with a Vision can venture within a Withering Zone and find a way to deal with it.

choices.text: I might be able to help with this.

response.speaker: Amir
response.text: But, you don't seem to carry a Vision...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry, {M#he}{F#she} may not have a Vision, but {M#he}{F#she}'s a real pro at using the power of the elements.

choices.text: I can also control the elements.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Tighnari, we found the lotuses you requested.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let me take a look... Hmm, good, very good. These are all excellent quality.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm glad you two came along, your exploration experience helped save me a lot of time here. It seems we even have enough time to stock up on other things I need...

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: Hey! Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Tighnari, someone's calling your name. They're dressed like a forest ranger.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, that's Amir and the others. But didn't they just set off not too long ago? What are they doing back so early?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's go find out what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm, it seems the rumors about you are true then. In that case... Alright, you two may accompany me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We typically only teach visitors how to identify The Withering as they're about to leave Gandharva Ville. We'll make an exception today and show you what it looks like up close.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Stop, don't move any further. Look there, in the distance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, where? Oh! Look, those plants have withered... That whole area is kinda gloomy. Even the air looks like it's filled with ash.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon doesn't like the look of this.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That is The Withering.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, Traveler, we're going to have to enter that Withering Zone. Once inside, we'll need to look for what we call Tumors of The Withering. If we eliminate those, then the area will be saved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Gotcha, let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Thank you. But I must warn you, don't push yourself. This is your first time handling this sort of thing, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Even with elemental powers, once you step inside the Withering Zone, you may experience extreme discomfort. If at any point it becomes too much, return outside the zone and take a breather. It could become a matter of life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You ready, then? Let's go!

talks.objective: Help Tighnari clear the Withering Zone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! That gloomy area over there looks like a Withering Zone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though Paimon's seen one before, it's still kinda scary...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright Traveler, we're about to enter the Withering Zone. Since you already have experience dealing with these things, you should already know what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But please remember, don't push yourself. If at any point it becomes too much, return outside the zone and take a breather. It could become a matter of life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You ready, then? Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did it! Everything's returning to normal now!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, thanks to you two, we were able to quickly restore this area back to normal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Tighnari? You make it sound like we did well, but why does Paimon have the feeling you're worried about something?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's that obvious, huh? Alright, it's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Recently, the rate at which Withering Zones appear has been increasing. Even though we were able to quickly clear that Withering Zone, it won't be long before another one appears.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If that simply meant more work for me, then that wouldn't be an issue... But it's far more severe than that. The Withering is leaving lasting effects on the rainforest itself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: For instance, even though we cleared out the Withering Zone, many of the plants that were affected will not recover.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This presents a crisis for the ecosystem itself. Many plants in the rainforest are already in decline, directly impacting the wildlife that depends on those plants.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And most disturbingly... as the appearances of Withering Zones have started to increase, Collei's case of Eleazar has also become more serious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm still not sure of the exact reason. However, I've received word from acquaintances at the Akademiya that similar cases are being reported for patients with other conditions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there no way to permanently get rid of The Withering?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No, none that we know of. The Withering has been recorded in Sumeru for millennia. It's said that it originates from the depths of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: By the way, have you heard of Irminsul before?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Irminsul is a tree located deep beneath the surface. Although it isn't like any tree we know in a biological sense, you can basically think of it as a large tree that grows downwards rather than upwards.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'm sure you've heard of Ley Lines, right? They're like the roots of Irminsul, spreading and extending from a massive cavern deep underground all the way up to the surface.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Spreading and extending, a massive cavern... Sounds a lot like what I saw when I lost consciousness in the cave.)

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ley Lines continually absorb the memories of this world, which are then funneled into Irminsul, allowing it to collect knowledge and wisdom from ancient times to present day.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The Dendro Archon is known as the God of Wisdom because her consciousness is directly connected to it. It is also said that the Dendro Archon's power is a manifestation of Irminsul.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: And as for The Withering, its emergence is related to a disease that's affecting it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh? You mean Irminsul is sick?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That's right. My ancestors learned of this from Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's familiars a long time ago, but even those mysterious creatures did not know of a cure for Irminsul.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'm afraid we rangers will be battling the Withering Zones here for a long time until a cure is found.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright, that's enough on this topic for the time being. Now that we've taken care of things here, it's time for us to head back to Gandharva Ville.

choices.text: I think I've heard it somewhere before.

dialogues.speaker: Amir
dialogues.text: Oh, Tighnari, you all made it back! How did it go?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Withering Zone you reported has been taken care of. No need to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, is that...?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh no! Haypasia!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong, Tighnari?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This Dusk Bird is Haypasia's designated courier for urgent news. You do remember her, don't you? She's the scholar you and Paimon were following when you first arrived in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, her! How could we forget! Uh, so did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let me see what's written in the letter first. Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what's it say? And what's with that weird expression on your face? Ugh, just let Paimon read it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, all Paimon sees are three squiggly lines...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, allow me to explain. After we brought you from Haypasia's cave to Gandharva Ville, Haypasia resumed her meditation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: She must have just finished. It's been nearly three days since she's had anything to eat, and it appears she's forgotten to prepare some rations. This letter is her asking us for help, we need to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? You mean she's been sitting there for three days!? Hey wait, how did you know all that from just a few lines on the paper?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, obviously because this has happened before... Last time she drew five lines, and by the time we found her... Ahem, well, I'd prefer not to remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Needless to say, Haypasia's been through worse, but we should still get to her as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I've got some emergency rations set aside for times like these. Paimon, Traveler, could you two bring these to her?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait, you want us to bring her the rations? But will {NICKNAME} be okay if her cave is still filled with that funny incense?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Let's find out. Here, {NICKNAME}, take a smell and see.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: So, how do you feel?

choices.text: Hmm, it's a light and refreshing fragrance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Really? You're not feeling even a little drowsy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But wait, how'd you know that {M#he}{F#she}'d be okay this time, Tighnari?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Back when we were clearing the Withering Zone, I observed that {M#he}{F#she} could adeptly manipulate the Dendro element. I knew then that {M#he}{F#she} would be fine.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, and if I may ask, when I was telling you two about Irminsul's Ley Lines, was what I described similar at all to what you saw when you were unconscious?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What I saw weren't hallucinations, were they?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That's correct, those weren't hallucinations at all, though I don't intend to apologize for deceiving you...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Because what you saw is of significant importance, not just for the nation of Sumeru, but the entire world of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: My forefathers were shown much favor by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. We took an oath to protect this nation together with her. Now that that duty has fallen to me, it was a part of my responsibilities to ascertain whether you could be entrusted with the fate of Sumeru.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Now, after seeing you in action with my own eyes, you have earned my confidence, and I no longer feel the need to hide any secrets from you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what exactly was it that I saw?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: When you passed out, your consciousness had connected directly with Irminsul. What you witnessed were actually real memories contained within Irminsul itself.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I could try to tell you more, but it would be better if you went to ask Haypasia instead. Her focus on meditation and use of Spirit Borneol are aimed at establishing a connection with Irminsul, just as you did.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that sounds nice and all, but will she really help us? Seriously, she completely ignored us the last time we tried talking to her!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That was because when you ran into her, she was in a special phase of her training. During that time, she must avoid communicating with others.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Please, wait here for a moment.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tighnari leaves for a few moments...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Here, take these. It's a meal I packed for Haypasia, as well as some other ingredients. I'm sure it'll come in handy.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Also, here's a letter that I would like you to give to her. Just show it to her, and she'll answer any questions you may have.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: No, I should be the one thanking you. You've both been a great help these last few days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't sweat it, we've helped others deal with similar situations before.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Wait, you've met other Forest Rangers before? I was planning to properly show you both how to identify The Withering before you left Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, since you two are experienced adventurers, come with me, I'm sure you'll both be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, please take good care of Haypasia.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'll go prepare Collei's medicine now. Using the Nilotpala Lotuses while they're still fresh will significantly boost their effectiveness.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Rest assured, Collei will recover quickly as long as she has her medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shhh! Collei's asleep! Let's come back once she's feeling better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Paimon was thinking all night about what happened with Collei, and still can't figure out what the problem might be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe she's in a better mood now... Let's go check on her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Tighnari, where exactly are we going to find this plant?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Nilotpala Lotuses can be found all over the rainforest, but it often grows right here around Gandharva Ville.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, given the name, it sounds like we should be looking for it in the water.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You are correct, the Nilotpala Lotus grows in the water. When fully matured, they look like giant blue flowers floating on the water's surface. Quite an attractive species, if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The large petals are actually the plant's leaves and sepals which surround a very small flower.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You should note that many of the plants found in Sumeru have names that are contrary to their species.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Take the Kalpalata, for example. The plant is not a lotus at all, but rather a vine. And then there's the Sumeru Rose, which is not a rose, and is completely contrary to its name...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, huh... okay then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Note to Paimon: never bring up the topic of flowers with Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we've gathered enough Nilotpala Lotuses. Let's head back to meet Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: First, we must locate any branches sustaining the Withering Zone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haypasia should still be in the cave. Let's go inside and see how she's doing!
